name: Mansi Thakar Jani
deck: Gujarat built stepwells and lakes to hold water through the dry months. Munsar Lake had been ignored for years. Four events later there are volunteers who call themselves Stepwell Guardians and check on the sites when nobody is watching.
description: Munsar Lake, the Saptamukhi stepwell and Valavav: four events across Gujarat, about seven hundred people, and volunteers trained to watch the sites after.

aims.h: Put the old water structures back in use
aims.p: Saptamukhi at Dabhoi, Valavav at Mahuva, Munsar Lake at Viramgam. They still hold water. Mostly they hold rubbish.
A clean-up crowd leaves the same evening. Local volunteers were trained to keep watch on a site after it does.

aims.h: Take the students to the well
aims.p: Heritage taught next to the thing itself, with sketching and a survey, rather than in a chapter about water conservation.

did: Ran four on-ground events across Mahuva, Dabhoi and Viramgam
Cleaned up Munsar Lake at Viramgam with local volunteers and the Ahmedabad Bike Riders Community
Ran awareness sessions and heritage talks at the Saptamukhi stepwell in Dabhoi, with live sketching
Took students from Sathara village to the Valavav stepwell
Documented the sites by drone and ground survey, and tested the water
Trained local volunteers as Stepwell Guardians
Began registering the group behind it as the Kachab Foundation

quotes.text: This initiative helped us see Munsar Lake in a new way. We had ignored it for years, but through this clean-up and awareness effort, we now understand its importance and feel responsible for keeping it clean.
quotes.speaker: Tejas Vejani

quotes.text: The Varso Jal Sanchay Abhiyan provided meaningful experiential learning for our students by connecting heritage with water conservation. The visit to Valavav stepwell enhanced their understanding of traditional water systems and instilled a sense of responsibility towards protecting such structures. Initiatives like this are crucial for shaping environmentally conscious youth.
quotes.speaker: Maheshwariben Ghoghari

quotes.text: Visiting Valavav stepwell and learning about its history was a new experience for us. It made us realize how important it is to protect these water structures and not throw waste around them.
quotes.speaker: A student at Sathara High School

quotes.text: Being part of the clean-up made me feel connected to our heritage. Small actions like this can bring real change if more people participate.
quotes.speaker: A clean-up volunteer

holes: The water at the heritage sites was tested. The readings are not in the report, so there is no before figure to hold the clean-ups against.

frames.alt: Schoolgirls seated on rugs on the paved edge of Munsar Lake in low morning light, facing a Varso Jal Sanchay banner, with carved stone blocks, a flagged temple and the far bank reflected in still water
